C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY.Summary: Ship the ongoing record-retirement operation and the first CodifiedIn / TaughtIn tagging so the RM-GOVERNED-PATH record can retire as fast as it grows. Extend the PaidBy derivation so validation cannot exit 0 while a live finding is eligible under that derivation; add a --retire command that stamps PaidBy, moves eligible entries to the retired sibling, updates the citation-index layer, and re-derives the live root's base / headroom / ceiling. Correct the rulings headroom multiplier from 2 to 7 (the findings cycle constant) in this bundle, argued against D28.1; after that one rewrite the clamp forbids a later raise. Validators read record XML through parseGraceXmlArtifact; writes stay surgical. Pays F180 and F181. Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30. Staged charter D34 (not yet flushed). Overturns C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2's NonGoal of zero historical CodifiedIn / TaughtIn tags.
C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY.Problem:
C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 split the record and shipped the ratchet. It did not ship the ongoing operation. D28 required that every entry have an observable retirement trigger and that enforcement ship with the structure, never after. The structure and the ratchet shipped; the operation shipped only as --split, which refuses once decisions.md is a stub (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:477-478).
F180, F181, and D34 live in the D30 buffer .ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md, not in findings.xml / rulings.xml. This spec does not flush them. D34 (ratified 2026-09-06) charters this bundle at position 4, ahead of C-ROADMAP-XML, and names four deliverables: a PaidBy feed, detection that uses the derivation, a retirement move, and the first CodifiedIn / TaughtIn tagging.
Measured 2026-09-06 at 67bc55cbfb7e7fc6f672012801780f3db517984d, reproducing collectPaidBy (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:372-410) against live plus retired chartered rows: the map has 24 F-tokens, all already retired; 0 live findings are eligible under that function as shipped. 0 of 214 live findings carry a stored <PaidBy> child; all 25 retired findings do. Validation reads only the stored child (:673) and bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts exits 0. collectPaidBy runs only in --split (:489). F180's claim that the same function maps 36 tokens of which 12 are live-eligible is not reproduced; those twelve tokens (F9.1, F100, F105, F108, F108.1, F108.2, F109.1, F112, F113, F125, F155.1, F157) occupy 477 lines of findings.xml but are not collectPaidBy-eligible. The hole this bundle closes is that detection ignores the derivation, the derivation itself misses archive-named Pays rows whose StatusText does not match /delivered|superseded/i and misses StatusText "Closed with" claims, and no command can move an eligible entry.
Zero of 60 live decisions carry CodifiedIn or TaughtIn (C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 NonGoal). Decisions therefore have no reachable trigger. This bundle overturns that NonGoal (CLAUDE.md rule 9): the tags and both resolution checks already ship; populating the first real tags is this work.
D28.1: eligibility carries no number so no number can be raised to pass it; a ceiling-exceeded failure names the retirement operation and must not name a config key as the remedy; the rejected shape was a line budget as sole enforcement, whose cheapest way out is a config edit (rulings.xml:1498-1506). Re-deriving a mis-sized formula is not that act. C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 sized rulings headroom as 2 times the median live H2 Decision (entry size). Staged F181 measured one session's arrival at four decisions against that two-entry headroom. The clamp min(previousCeiling, newBase + newHeadroom) would make that split-time ceiling permanent, so the formula correction ships in the same bundle as the clamp. This spec answers F181 here, argued against D28.1, and does not leave arrival-rate sizing as a NonGoal.
The three record validators each carry a regex parser and bypass parseGraceXmlArtifact (src/artifact/xml.ts, LINKS M-GRAMMAR). Consolidating reads onto that layer is in scope. serializeGraceXmlDocument hoists inter-element whitespace and is not a whole-file writer for this corpus; writes stay surgical. No new XML library.

Goals.Goal: A PaidBy feed. The retirement script derives a payer map and writes a <PaidBy> child onto each live finding the map names, with the payer equal to the archived C-* directory. The feed runs as part of --retire (stamp then move in one invocation) and as a --stamp-paid-by mode that writes the children and does not move. It does not hook ngrace gate archive or lifecycle finish: this record is this repository's, validation stays in scripts/, and src/ is not in scope. After a paying bundle archives, the next validate:record-retirement run goes red until --retire is invoked. That is the observable trigger.

Detection that uses the derivation. bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts (no mutating argv) exits non-zero when a live finding is in the payer map with an archive-directory payer, even if that finding has no stored <PaidBy> child. A stored <PaidBy> that names an archive directory remains an error (shipped). One error per finding, naming the archive event. Planted refuse: a live finding, payer archived, no stored child, must fail; adding the child without moving must still fail; moving to the retired sibling must pass.

A retirement move. argv --retire on scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts stamps PaidBy from the derivation, moves every eligible live finding, every live decision that carries a resolving CodifiedIn or TaughtIn, and every live registry row whose name equals an archive directory, to the matching retired sibling; sets status="retired" on the moved element; updates the matching decisions.xml Entry layer from live to retired; and re-derives the live root's base, headroom, and ceiling as the ceiling-ruling Constraint specifies. --split remains and still refuses a stub. --retire is not a validate:ci member (it mutates).

First CodifiedIn / TaughtIn tagging. This bundle populates the first real tags on live Decision elements that verify at execution, then --retire moves them. C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2's NonGoal of zero historical tags is overturned here, not silently. D27.1 is the first candidate by its own text once it is a live Decision; it is not live at this spec's writing (staged buffer only) and this bundle does not flush it. The first live tag this bundle writes is D24 against C-REWORK-CIRCUIT, if it still verifies at execution (both directions of T-001 and T-003 in src/grace-cursor.test.ts). D24 remains a candidate to verify, not a fact to restate, until that re-run (D28.1, F123). Additional live decisions that verify the same way in the same apply may be tagged; they are not required and are not enumerated.

Ceiling ruling, stated and argued against D28.1. Re-deriving base / headroom / ceiling after a successful --retire is a snapshot of the new live population under the formulas. The forbidden act is occupancy red then increasing a persisted number until green, without a move; that remains forbidden. The rulings multiplier 2 measured entry size and not cycle arrival (staged F181). This bundle replaces it with 7, the findings cycle constant already shipped by C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2, so both content genres size headroom as one cycle of median entries. Findings, registry, and index formulas are unchanged. The clamp min(previousCeiling, newBase + newHeadroom) holds for every later --retire and for findings / registry / index on this bundle's first rewrite. For rulings only, this bundle's first production attribute rewrite may persist the formula ceiling even when it exceeds the split-time ceiling, because that ceiling was computed from the uncorrected multiplier; after that write the clamp binds. A later red is cured only by a move. The failure message continues to name --retire / move to the retired sibling and must not name a config key or the multiplier.

Payer derivation, replacing the delivered|superseded filter. The archive directory is the event D28.1 names. A live finding's payer is the first C-* name, in this order, for which that name is a directory under .ngrace/changes/archive/: (1) an F-token in the Pays child of a chartered Row in registry.xml or registry-retired.xml whose name equals that directory; (2) an F-token in a Closed-with claim in that same row's StatusText; (3) an F-token in an archived spec.xml sentence matching the shipped /\bthe paid findings?\b/i regex (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:33, :397-407). Closed-with grammar: after XML-decode and whitespace-flatten of StatusText, replace each markdown citation wrapper [TOKEN](#slug) with TOKEN so the house form [F100](#f100)–[F105](#f105) reduces to F100–F105; then a clause matching /\bClosed with\b/i through the next period; F-tokens via the shipped F_TOKEN_RE; a range is two F-tokens separated by U+2013, U+2014, or ASCII hyphen-minus whose last integer segments form an inclusive numeric range and whose prefix otherwise matches (so F100–F105 expands to F100 through F105). Without that reduction the two F-tokens have ](#f100) between them and the spec's own range example does not meet the record. Mere mention of an F-token in an archived spec, in a Charter, or in StatusText outside a Closed-with clause is not payment (C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2 stands on that half). A live chartered row whose name is not an archive directory does not pay. Do not enumerate the eligible set in this spec (D30).

--retire command. bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire reads the production record under docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/ (or an argv directory, fixture-safe: argv naming a fixture path does not read the repository's record files). It stamps missing <PaidBy> children from the derivation, moves eligible elements as the Goal describes, writes status="retired", updates decisions.xml Entry layer, re-derives live-root attributes, and exits 0. A second --retire with nothing eligible is a no-op exit 0 and must not rewrite ceiling. Bodies are moved, not rewritten, except the status attribute, the PaidBy stamp, and wrap. prove-record-preservation.ts still exits 0 after a move. --stamp-paid-by writes PaidBy children only. --split still refuses a stub. Production validate (no mutating argv) never writes.

Ceiling ruling, the act this bundle performs, argued against D28.1. After a successful --retire that moved at least one element, persist on every live root (not only the genre that moved, so a findings-only first move still rewrites rulings under the corrected multiplier): base = live size at that moment (line count of findings.xml / rulings.xml / decisions.xml; live-row count of registry.xml); headroom = findings: 7 times the median live Finding element line count; rulings: 7 times the median live H2 Decision element line count (was 2; corrected this bundle); registry: 15 live-row slots; index: 40 lines; formulaCeiling = base + headroom. For findings, registry, and index: ceiling = min(previously persisted ceiling, formulaCeiling). For rulings on this bundle's first production attribute rewrite: ceiling = formulaCeiling, even if that exceeds the split-time persisted ceiling; that exception is the formula correction and is not available on later invocations. For every later --retire, including later rulings rewrites: ceiling = min(previously persisted ceiling, formulaCeiling). If the clamp binds, persist headroom = previousCeiling - base so the three attributes stay a consistent snapshot. This is not raising a number to pass: the new rulings multiplier is the findings cycle constant, not a function of the current occupancy, and a later red cannot be cured by changing it. The only permitted production writer of base, headroom, and ceiling is --retire after a successful move (--split wrote the initial snapshot and now refuses). Validate continues to compare occupancy to the persisted ceiling only; it does not recompute headroom from the current median on every run. Ceiling-exceeded failure text names --retire / move to the retired sibling, never a config key and never the multiplier, and says raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy. Do not pin a scalar count of a record file into this Constraint (D30).
